entities.summary:
Channel One Russia is a major Russian federal television channel headquartered at the Ostankino Technical Center in Moscow, emerging from Soviet Central Television’s successor structures and taking its post-Soviet identity in the 1990s (commonly dated 1995 in institutional listings).

As a partly state-influenced broadcaster, Channel One has been central to national news framing, entertainment, and political communication under Yeltsin and Putin eras. Ostankino’s towers and studios symbolise the continuity of Russian mass television power.

Channel One illustrates how post-Soviet media hybrids combine commercial formats with state strategic messaging.
